entries.test: Public AI deployment audits with measured costs and returns, and reproducible task-cost accounting, would test the claimed impossibility and its proposed causes.
entries.note: The universal claim can be contradicted by a documented counterexample.
The source says failures can be hard to predict, not that they are unpredictable. The failure claim is explicitly a possibility.
Pricing transparency is observable, but the claim also asserts Microsoft's private intention to boost growth by concealment.

entries.test: Subscription prices, disclosed token costs, usage allowances and provider cost accounts would show whether every subscriber is subsidized and denied actual cost information.
entries.note: The claim covers every user, including light users.

entries.test: AI startup financial statements and supplier spending would show whether all are unprofitable because of inference costs and send all venture funding to Anthropic and OpenAI.
entries.note: The normalization weakens the explicit assertion that literally every penny goes to those two suppliers.

entries.test: Public financial disclosures available at publication would show whether any AI lab demonstrated profitability attributable to operating its own infrastructure.
entries.note: The firm claim concerns the absence of evidence; the infrastructure savings are only presented as possible.

entries.test: Anthropic subscription allowances and equivalent token prices would test the ratio, while public inference revenue and cost disclosures would test the claimed absence of profitability evidence.
entries.note: The token dollar figure needs to be distinguished from Anthropic's underlying operating cost.
The source says every other AI company, not merely other companies. Its explanation depends on their private knowledge and motives.

entries.test: Enterprise billing notices, contract changes and employer AI-use policies would establish the Q1 transition, its coverage and its relationship to reported spending problems.
entries.note: The source gives two causes of the problem, without establishing that the CEO pressure preceded the billing change.

entries.test: Representative user surveys and usage-cost studies would test whether an overwhelming majority were conditioned to disregard token costs and consequently used services uneconomically.
entries.note: Most weakens overwhelming majority, and the normalization omits complete disconnection from costs.

entries.test: Repeated task evaluations and comparable task-cost histories would test the asserted unreliability, inconsistency and absence of declining costs.
entries.note: The surrounding discussion supplies a practical reading based on task performance and cost.

entries.test: Matched-task comparisons across model generations would show whether increased token consumption outweighs lower token prices and raises total inference cost.

entries.note: The source says the deception stopped working, not that the conspiracy stopped. The allegation also depends on a shared intention to deceive.

entries.test: Industry investment totals, company cash expenditures, matched-task costs and reliability evaluations over the stated four years would test the comparisons.
entries.note: The normalization extracts the factual comparisons without the accompanying insults.

entries.test: Comparable AI task-cost measurements from June 2023 through June 2026 would show whether costs rose and were continuing to rise or remain flat.
entries.note: Today refers to the publication date.
Calling the comments lies asserts knowing deception, beyond whether the cost prediction was accurate.

entries.test: Comparable deployed-workload costs on Blackwell and Vera Rubin versus predecessor hardware would show whether either reduced AI costs.
entries.note: This combines a historical claim with an undated forecast; the timing reflects the forecast.

entries.test: Documented reductions in comparable AI task costs attributable to any named chip platform or DeepSeek would contradict the forecast.
entries.note: No deadline is stated.
The normalization removes don't appear from the cost premise. The passage offers a tentative inference about viability rather than a causal mechanism.
Far worse and largest misallocation express comparative judgments without an agreed measure of harm or waste.
The explanation rests on NVIDIA's alleged private priorities.

entries.test: Documented economically useful operation or reuse of infrastructure left after an AI investment collapse would contradict the forecast.
entries.note: The surrounding discussion gives redemption arc a concrete infrastructure-reuse meaning.

entries.test: Public workload inventories and deployment studies would show the breadth and practical significance of non-AI uses for GPU-filled AI data centers.
entries.note: The next sentence explicitly allows limited scientific and analytics applications.

entries.test: AI data-center construction accounts and operating financial histories would show upfront costs and whether any achieved profits within their first five or six years.
entries.note: Operating profitability and recovery of original capital are distinct parts of the claim.

entries.test: Comparable GPU-rack operating bills and data-center completion and power-connection costs in June 2031 versus June 2026 would test the forecast.
entries.note: The five-year horizon runs from publication.

entries.test: Engineering plans and actual conversion accounts would show whether repurposing AI data centers requires gutting them and discarding most original capital investment.
entries.note: This is a testable engineering prediction about conversion, rather than an inaccessible historical counterfactual.

entries.test: Public AI-service financial statements available at publication would show whether a demonstrated profitable business model existed.
entries.note: Appears here describes the visible evidence for an existing business outcome.

entries.test: Actual full-cost pricing, customer retention and affordability data would show whether demand depends on subsidies and whether most users can afford unsubsidized service.
entries.note: The possible future is hedged, but the subsidy dependence and unaffordability are asserted.

entries.test: After a recognizable AI investment bust, public startup financings, approved token budgets or data-center debt deals would contradict the categorical prediction.
entries.note: The forecast requires the stated bubble-burst event.
Subsidies are factual, but the conclusion that product value is flimsy is a judgment of worth.
Only way asserts that the bubble could not have formed in a counterfactual world without deception.

entries.test: Auditable AI deployments with quantified benefits exceeding all associated costs would contradict the claimed absence of measurable returns.
entries.note: The heading explicitly explains the alleged measurement failure through the alleged absence of returns.
The denial of AI displacement is separately testable, but the combined claim assigns private motives to every company citing AI for layoffs.

entries.test: Documented workplace deployments and staffing records would show whether AI performs complete jobs or replaces employees beyond the conceded contract-role exceptions.
entries.note: The normalization preserves the explicit exception.
The full paragraph supports the walkback clause omitted from the excerpt. Fundraising and walkbacks are observable, but knowing deception is an additional private-state claim.
Statements and release dates are checkable, but a later release does not establish that the earlier statement was knowingly false.
Willing to believe presents a possibility rather than a firm finding.

entries.test: Comparative software defect, maintenance and quality data together with Anthropic and Cursor spending records would test the asserted overall economic effects.
entries.note: Appears qualifies an assessment of existing observable outcomes, rather than assigning a future probability.
Mark is a sweeping insult rather than an operational claim about each user.
The explanation makes a judgment of product quality the cause of fundraising strategy.

entries.test: Publicly auditable AI deployments showing financial benefits exceeding total implementation and operating costs would contradict the claim.
entries.note: The normalization extracts the factual premise from the source's causal sentence.

entries.test: Task-complexity evaluations and comparisons across infrastructure investment levels would test changes in speed, accuracy, value and the number of tasks supported.
entries.note: Number of tasks can mean capacity or volume; range specifically means diversity. The normalization also turns can speed up into speed up.

entries.test: Public operational evaluations demonstrating reliable LLM execution of a defined task without human supervision would contradict the universal claim.
entries.note: The plain reading concerns autonomous operational reliability.
This states the author's required standard for an acceptable product.
